_docs: Justice dialogue voice templates. Extracted from justice.js (Steve 2026-10-07). DIALOGUE ONLY — the knowledge gating (unwitnessed crimes never named), condition evaluation, and template selection stay in JS. Variables: {name}, {chargeWord}, {ChargeWord} (capitalized). Conditions in 'when' are matched against the speaker's context: close (trust >= 40), wary (cautious/withdrawn), bold (bold/intense), seriousType (strongest witnessed crime type).

attack.text: {name} plants themself in your way, jaw set. "You put hands on one of ours. That doesn't wash off with an apology — but an apology is where it starts."
{name} waits until the fire's low and it's just you two. "I saw what happened. I'm not here to fight — I'm here because next time, someone won't ask first."
{name} looks sick. "I told them you wouldn't — I said that, out loud, to people. Don't make me the fool here. Fix it."

{name} doesn't wait for a quiet moment. "You put hands on one of ours — in front of everyone, that's why it's me and not the whole fire. Say how you make it right, or we skip to the part where you don't."
{name} finds you at the edge of the firelight. "I liked you. That's the part that stings — I actually liked you. So tell me the hands thing was a one-time stupid, and mean it."

generic.text: {name} steps close. "Something's off and everyone's felt it. I drew the short straw — so here I am. Talk to me before the village decides it doesn't need to."
{name} sits down next to you like nothing's wrong, which is how you know everything is. "People are talking. I wanted you to hear it from me first."
{name} catches your eye across the fire and tilts their head — follow me. Away from everyone: "I'm asking as a friend, not the village. What happened?"
{name} plants themself square in your path. "Something's rotten and everyone's smelling it. I'm not leaving until you name it — or it gets named for you."
{name} catches you alone by the water. "People are keeping score now. I don't know of what yet. You want to tell me before they finish counting?"

murder.text: {name} steps in front of you. "We know what you did. Say it wasn't you — go on, try." Their hands are shaking. Not from fear. "You pay it back, or you go. Those are the choices."
{name} finds you alone, away from the fire. "Tell me it wasn't you." A pause — you can see them hoping. "Please. Tell me it wasn't you."
{name} doesn't raise their voice. That's how you know it's serious. "Someone's dead. And everyone knows whose hands. Talk."
{name} won't come closer than arm's length. "Someone's dead. I keep thinking about who'll say the words at the fire. It shouldn't be me. But here I am. Talk."
{name} says it flat, no heat, which is worse. "Dead is dead. There's no version where we all just move past it. You get one chance to say your piece — take it."

theft.text: {name} blocks your path. "We need to talk about the stores. About what you've been taking." A few others are watching, not approaching. "Make it right, or leave. Your call."
{name} won't look at you. "The stores. I covered for you once — told them it was a miscount. Don't make me a liar too."
{name} corners you by the stores, voice low. "Count it with me. Right now. If I'm wrong I'll say so in front of everyone."
{name} keeps their voice down, eyes on the stores. "Things keep walking off. I don't want it to be you. Give me a reason it isn't — a good one, fast."
{name} doesn't soften it. "The stores feed everyone. You steal from the stores, you steal from kids. Fix it loud enough that everyone hears, or don't bother fixing it."

summons.fallback: {name} looks around the fire. "No more talking around it. There'll be a moot — all of it, in the open."

heat.text: "It's past asking," {name} says. "The fire hears {chargeWord} — tonight, in the open."
{name} won't meet your eyes. "I was going to talk to you. It's past that now. The moot hears {chargeWord} — in the open."
{name} doesn't bother with preamble. "A moot. {ChargeWord}. In the open."
{name} keeps their distance, hands visible. "Heat's too high for talking quiet anymore. {ChargeWord} — the fire hears it tonight, in the open."
{name} raises their voice so the whole fire hears. "No more quiet words! {ChargeWord} gets a moot — tonight, in the open, everyone."
{name} looks hollow. "Someone's dead and the village is coming apart. {ChargeWord} — the moot hears it tonight. In the open. No more waiting."

refused.text: {name} stands, and the fire goes quiet around them. "No more talking around it. {ChargeWord} gets a moot — all of it, in the open. You said no to me. Say it to everyone."
{name} says it low, and the low carries. "There'll be a moot. {ChargeWord} — in the open. I asked you quiet. You chose loud."
{name} looks sick saying it. "I asked you as —" A breath. "There's a moot. {ChargeWord}, in the open. I didn't want this."
{name}'s voice doesn't shake. That's how you know. "A moot. For the killing. In the open, where everyone has to hear it."
{name} doesn't dress it up. "You put hands on one of ours. The moot hears {chargeWord} — all of it, in the open."
{name} looks around the fire. "The stores. The counts. All of it — in the open. There's a moot."
{name} keeps their voice level. "Threats stop working when everyone hears them. A moot — in the open."
{name} looks around the fire. "No more talking around it. There'll be a moot — all of it, in the open."

silence.text: {name} waited two days for your answer. None came — so the question goes to everyone. "{ChargeWord}, in the open. Be there, or don't. It happens either way."
{name} doesn't look at you when they say it. "I waited. Two days. The moot hears {chargeWord} — all of it, in the open."
{name} stands. "Silence is an answer. Fine. Here's ours: a moot. {ChargeWord}, in the open, where silence doesn't work."
{name} speaks to the fire, not to you. "Two days I waited for an answer. The question's bigger than one person now. {ChargeWord}, in the open — the moot decides."
{name} doesn't ask twice — they already did. "You had two days. You chose quiet. So here's loud: a moot. {ChargeWord}, in the open, tonight."
{name} stands slowly. "Silence had its chance. {ChargeWord} goes to the fire now — all of it, in the open, where silence doesn't count as an answer."
